landmarks.name: Niobe Planitia
landmarks.origin: Greek; her 12 children killed by Artemis and Apollo.

quote.text: The Niobe Planitia eruption produced about 17 square miles (45 square kilometers) of rock, which would fill 54,000 Olympic swimming pools.
The geological changes Herrick found occurred in Atla Regio, a vast highland region near Venus' equator that hosts two of the planet's largest volcanoes, Ozza Mons and Maat Mons.
Its circular shape and size (2100 km or 1302 miles in diameter) make Artemis the largest corona identified to date on the surface of Venus.

landmarks.name: Lakshmi Planum
landmarks.origin: Indian goddess of love and war.

quote.text: Lakshmi Planum is an elevated plateau plain that is bounded on all sides by mountain chains.
In 1963 Alpha Regio was the first feature on Venus to be identified from Earth based radar.
The Maxwell Montes are the highest mountains on Venus, rising up to 11 km above the mean planetary surface.

landmarks.name: Maat Mons
landmarks.origin: Ancient Egyptian goddess of truth and justice.

quote.text: A new study found one of Maat Mons' vents became enlarged and changed shape over an eight-month period in 1991, indicating an eruptive event occurred.
Gula Mons, a 3 kilometer (1.9 mile) high volcano, is located at approximately 22 degrees north latitude, 359 degrees east longitude in western Eistla Regio.
At 280 km diameter, Mead is the largest impact crater on Venus.

landmarks.name: Sacajawea Patera
landmarks.origin: Shoshoni Indian woman who served as an interpreter for the Lewis & Clark expedition to the Pacific Northwest (1786-1812).

quote.text: The formation of Sacajawea is thought to be related to the drainage and collapse of a large magma chamber.

landmarks.name: Sapas Mons
landmarks.origin: Phoenician commerce, travel, and messenger goddess.

quote.text: Sapas Mons, a volcano 400 kilometers (248 miles) across and 1.5 kilometers (0.9 mile) high is located at approximately 8 degrees north latitude, 188 degrees east longitude, on the western edge of Atla Regio.

landmarks.name: Cleopatra
landmarks.origin: Egyptian queen, notable for love affairs with Julius Caesar and Mark Anthony (69-30 B.C.).

quote.text: Cleopatra is a double-ring impact basin about 100 kilometers (62 miles) in diameter and 2.5 kilometers (1.5 miles) deep.

Regio.meaning: A large area marked by reflectivity or color distinctions from adjacent areas, or a broad geographic region

Linea.meaning: A dark or bright elongate marking, may be curved or straight

Patera.meaning: An irregular crater, or a complex one with scalloped edges
